items.action: Prioritize NetScaler Gateway and AAA virtual servers with SAML authentication enabled; apply the fixed build (14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28, 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.41, or 13.1-FIPS/NDcPP 13.1-37.282) or Citrix's interim mitigation immediately. Run Citrix's IoC check script on exposed appliances — a clean result is not definitive proof of non-compromise.
items.details: Disclosed by Citrix on October 3 after exploitation reports, with Bishop Fox and watchTowr credited for discovery — watchTowr reproduced it within hours on a NetScaler honeypot. watchTowr's head of threat intelligence told The Register that a single crafted request can knock an appliance offline, and suspects the bug is being used to purposefully crash machines to speed up exploitation of the earlier CVE-2026-88771 RCE chain.
items.summary: A memory-overflow bug (CVE-2026-88779) in NetScaler ADC/Gateway deployments using SAML as service provider or identity provider allows denial of service with a single crafted request. Exploited in the wild before the patch existed; CISA added it to KEV on October 4 and ordered federal agencies to patch by October 7.
items.title: Citrix NetScaler SAML zero-day (CVE-2026-88779) crashing appliances, CISA sets Oct 7 patch deadline

items.action: Disable the btest service if it is not in use, update RouterOS to the latest firmware immediately, and monitor internet-facing routers for signs of scanning or compromise.
items.details: The flaw sits in the btest (bandwidth-test) service, which fails to enforce authentication checks. Researchers and CISA report automated scanning of internet-exposed MikroTik devices attempting to exploit it. Full exploit methods have not been publicly disclosed, and it is unclear exactly which builds are affected.
items.summary: A missing-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-67277) in MikroTik RouterOS's btest service lets unauthenticated attackers read kernel memory and crash routers. CISA confirmed active exploitation and placed it in the KEV catalog; kernel memory disclosure could expose sensitive data or enable deeper compromise.
items.title: MikroTik RouterOS pre-auth flaw (CVE-2026-67277) under active exploitation

items.action: Upgrade Camunda 7 to 7.24.15 or later and restrict network reachability of the Admin web application; audit environments that provision administrators via group mappings rather than the default admin group.
items.details: The vulnerability is triggered only in a specific configuration state: the direct administrator group appears empty even though administrators are configured elsewhere (e.g., alternative group mappings). Published October 5; KEV/EPSS status not yet established and no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, but advisory analysis treats reachable instances as high-priority exposure.
items.summary: Camunda 7 versions 7.24.0 through 7.24.14 carry an incorrect-authorization flaw (CVE-2026-77226, CVSS 8.1) in the setup endpoint that can let a remote attacker establish administrator access without credentials, then alter workflow definitions or disrupt the engine.
items.title: Camunda 7 setup endpoint allows unauthenticated admin access (CVE-2026-77226)

items.action: If you share suppliers, customers, or data with Onsemi, review third-party exposure, check dark-web monitoring for your domain, and treat the leak-site listing as an unconfirmed claim until the company responds.
items.details: The listing was discovered on October 5 via ransomware.live tracking of Qilin's dark-web blog; no data volume, exfiltration details, or encryption confirmation accompanied the report. Qilin is one of the most active RaaS groups in 2026.
items.summary: The Qilin ransomware group added Onsemi, the semiconductor manufacturer, to its leak site on October 5. The listing is a threat-actor claim only — no official statement or independent confirmation of intrusion or exfiltration exists yet.
items.title: Qilin claims attack on semiconductor maker Onsemi

items.action: Monitor dark-web channels for the named credential sets and rotate any exposed API keys; treat the claimed data volumes as unverified but assume the worst for the RSA key and database credentials.
items.details: Infomedia A/S is a Danish media-monitoring hub serving clients including the EU Parliament and A.P. Møller-Mærsk. The claim, indexed from the group's public post on October 5, includes SQL Server 'sa' credentials for the Opoint CRM database, an RSA private key for the Export Data API, financial records tied to Danske Bank, and salary specifications for over 100 employees in Denmark and Estonia.
items.summary: The Aurora ransomware group claimed Infomedia A/S, a Danish media-monitoring company, on October 5 — alleging ~30 GB of exfiltrated data including financial records, database credentials, and a private API key. The claim is unverified.
items.title: Aurora ransomware claims Danish media monitor Infomedia, alleges 30 GB haul

items.action: Check dark-web monitoring for any exposure linked to your organization if you deal with Turn5; treat the leak-site claim as unverified until the company confirms.
items.details: Turn5 (turn5.com) is a Pennsylvania-based automotive aftermarket retailer reporting about $84.4M in revenue with 300–500 employees. The claim, published to the group's Tor leak site on October 5 and indexed via ransomware.live, covers 328 GB across 26,503 files and 446 folders.
items.summary: The Global Secret Group ransomware operation claimed Turn5, a US auto-parts retailer, on October 5, alleging 328 GB of encrypted/exfiltrated data across 26,503 files. The claim is unverified.
items.title: Global Secret Group claims 328 GB theft from auto-parts retailer Turn5

items.action: For DFIR and insider-risk teams: review social-engineering awareness for staff with access to classified systems, and ensure mobile-device and messaging-app forensics capabilities cover encrypted chats, deleted artifacts, and cloud backups.
items.details: The sailor was arrested in Coimbatore; the case is being investigated by the Andhra Pradesh Police Counter Intelligence wing, which is examining the suspect's electronic communications and the classification of information allegedly transmitted to a suspected Pakistani intelligence operative.
items.summary: An Indian Navy sailor was arrested in Coimbatore in an alleged Pakistan-linked honey-trap espionage case involving leaked defence information, per the October 5 India cyber brief. Investigators are forensically examining devices and encrypted communications — a reminder that modern espionage cases are now DFIR investigations.
items.title: Navy sailor arrested in alleged Pakistan-linked honey-trap espionage case

items.action: Anyone receiving a 'digital arrest' call should disconnect immediately and report via the 1930 helpline or the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal; no legitimate agency conducts investigations over video calls demanding money transfers.
items.details: South Delhi Cyber Police arrested two men after a businessman reported being coerced over WhatsApp video by fraudsters posing as law-enforcement officials into transferring ₹6 lakh. Tracing the beneficiary infrastructure revealed at least 10 linked cybercrime complaints, transactions approaching ₹50 lakh, and suspected international links — per the October 5 India cyber brief.
items.summary: A Delhi digital-arrest case where a businessman lost ₹6 lakh to fraudsters posing as officials over WhatsApp video led police to a ₹50-lakh money trail across 10 complaints — with suspected international links.
items.title: Delhi digital-arrest bust: ₹6-lakh case unravels ₹50-lakh trail across 10 complaints

items.action: Internet-facing SharePoint infrastructure should be inventoried, patched, and actively hunted for historical compromise — not merely version-checked. Indian government, BFSI, and critical-infrastructure teams should assume residual risk from these old flaws.
items.details: Researchers report the China-linked cluster (also tracked as Longlegs/Storm-2603) continues exploiting Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities against a water utility, a telecom provider, a government body, and a university — and has previously been observed targeting organisations in India. The attackers use compromised SharePoint environments to disable security controls before deploying ransomware.
items.summary: The China-linked Warlock ransomware cluster continues exploiting old Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities against critical infrastructure — including organisations in India — using compromised SharePoint servers to disable defences and stage ransomware.
items.title: Warlock ransomware keeps exploiting SharePoint flaws against critical infra, India in the blast radius
